slot.brief: Ask the shape/hybridisation of XeF4 and XeOF4-type species; count lone pairs via VSEPR and pick correct geometry option.

stem: Which option correctly gives the molecular shapes, lone-pair counts on Xe, and hybridisations in XeOF₄ and XeO₂F₂? Treat each multiple bond as one electron domain.
options: XeOF₄: trigonal bipyramidal, 0 lone pairs, sp³d; XeO₂F₂: tetrahedral, 1 lone pair, sp³
XeOF₄: square pyramidal, 1 lone pair, sp³d²; XeO₂F₂: seesaw, 1 lone pair, sp³d
XeOF₄: square pyramidal, 1 lone pair, sp³d; XeO₂F₂: seesaw, 1 lone pair, sp³d²
XeOF₄: octahedral, 1 lone pair, sp³d²; XeO₂F₂: seesaw, 0 lone pairs, sp³d

verdicts.working: XeOF₄ has 5 bonding domains and 1 lone pair on Xe: square-pyramidal shape, sp³d². XeO₂F₂ has 4 bonding domains and 1 lone pair: seesaw shape, sp³d.

working:
XeOF₄: 5 bonding domains + 1 lone pair → AX₅E; square pyramidal, sp³d².
XeO₂F₂: 4 bonding domains + 1 lone pair → AX₄E; seesaw, sp³d.

Independent check: XeOF₄ has 5 bonding domains and 1 lone pair on Xe: square-pyramidal shape, sp³d². XeO₂F₂ has 4 bonding domains and 1 lone pair: seesaw shape, sp³d.
solution:
XeOF₄ has 5 bonding domains and 1 lone pair, so it is AX₅E with square-pyramidal shape and sp³d² hybridisation.
XeO₂F₂ has 4 bonding domains and 1 lone pair, so it is AX₄E with seesaw shape and sp³d hybridisation.
Thus, the correct choice is (B).
